column1: 1:1|Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus,|Keeps divine commissioning and the promise as the apostolic message's horizon.
1:2|to Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.|Retains affection, kinship and threefold blessing.
1:3|I thank God, whom I serve as my ancestors did, with a clean conscience, as I constantly remember you in my prayers night and day.|Keeps ancestral continuity, conscience and unceasing remembrance.
1:4|Remembering your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.|Preserves grief remembered and anticipated joy.

1:5|I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am convinced, lives in you as well.|Keeps both women by name and the dwelling metaphor across generations.
1:6|For this reason I remind you to fan into flame God's gift that is in you through the laying on of my hands.|Retains rekindling image, gift and embodied commissioning.
1:7|For God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power, love and self-control.|Preserves the contrast and all three positive qualities.

1:8|So do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord or of me, his prisoner. Instead, share in suffering for the good news, relying on God's power.|Keeps imprisonment, shared suffering and divine capacity.

1:9|He saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to his own purpose and grace, given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times.|Preserves salvation/call, denial of works and pretemporal grace.

1:10|This grace has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the good news.|Keeps appearance, death's defeat and illumination of life.
1:11|For this good news I was appointed a herald, apostle and teacher.|Retains all three appointed roles.

1:12|That is why I suffer these things. But I am not ashamed, because I know the one I have trusted and am convinced that he is able to guard what I entrusted to him until that day.|Keeps suffering, personal trust and the deposit's direction as one plausible reading.
1:13|Hold to the pattern of sound words you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.|Preserves health metaphor, pattern and two Christ-located virtues.
1:14|Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.|Keeps entrusted treasure and indwelling divine help.
1:15|You know that everyone in Asia turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.|Retains the sweeping regional claim and both named examples.
1:16|May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain.|Keeps household blessing, repeated aid and imprisonment.
1:17|Instead, when he was in Rome, he searched diligently for me and found me.|Preserves named city and persistent search.
1:18|May the Lord grant him mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know very well how much service he rendered in Ephesus.|Keeps the doubled Lord expression, future day and named place.
2:1|You then, my child, be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus.|Retains kinship and passive divine strengthening.
2:2|Entrust what you heard from me through many witnesses to faithful people who will be qualified to teach others also.|Keeps four generations of transmission and multiple witnesses.
2:3|Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.|Retains military identity and hardship.
2:4|No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in ordinary civilian affairs, so as to please the one who enlisted him.|Keeps entanglement and commanding officer imagery.
2:5|Likewise, an athlete is not crowned unless competing according to the rules.|Preserves competition, rule and crown.
2:6|The hardworking farmer should be the first to receive a share of the crops.|Keeps labor, priority and agricultural yield.
2:7|Think about what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.|Preserves human reflection and divine understanding together.
2:8|Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead and descended from David, according to my good news.|Keeps resurrection, Davidic ancestry and personal stewardship.
2:9|For it I suffer hardship, even chains like a criminal. But God's word is not chained.|Preserves real imprisonment and the pointed chain wordplay.
2:10|Therefore, I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may obtain the salvation in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.|Keeps endurance, election and salvation's full goal.
2:11|This saying is trustworthy: If we died with him, we will also live with him;|Retains first parallel conditional promise.
2:12|if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he will also deny us;|Keeps promise and warning in matching clauses.
2:13|if we are unfaithful, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself.|Preserves divine constancy and its self-related basis without making faithlessness harmless.
2:14|Remind them of these things, solemnly warning them before the Lord not to fight over words. Such arguments do no good and ruin those who listen.|Keeps formal warning and destructive effect.
2:15|Make every effort to present yourself to God as approved, a worker with no cause for shame who cuts the word of truth straight.|Retains tested laborer and difficult straight-cutting metaphor.
2:16|Avoid profane empty chatter, for those who engage in it will advance into greater ungodliness,|Keeps avoidance and ironic progress.
2:17|and their talk will spread like gangrene. Hymenaeus and Philetus are among them.|Preserves bodily disease image and both names.
2:18|They have missed the mark concerning the truth, saying the resurrection has already happened, and they overturn the faith of some.|Keeps target-missing, false timing and real damage.

2:19|Nevertheless, God's firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are his,” and, “Let everyone who names the Lord's name turn away from unrighteousness.”|Preserves foundation, seal and both quotations.
2:20|In a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay; some are for honorable use and some for dishonorable use.|Keeps material range and opposed purposes.

2:21|Therefore, if anyone cleanses themselves from these things, they will be a vessel for honorable use—made holy, useful to the master and prepared for every good work.|Preserves vessel metaphor, cleansing and three results.
2:22|Flee youthful desires and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.|Keeps flight/pursuit and communal setting.
2:23|Reject foolish and ignorant controversies, knowing that they breed quarrels.|Retains intellectual evaluation and birth image.
2:24|The Lord's slave must not quarrel but must be gentle toward everyone, able to teach and patient when wronged,|Keeps slave status and three nonviolent teaching qualities.
2:25|correcting opponents with gentleness, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to knowledge of the truth|Preserves correction, humility and divine gift.
2:26|and that they may come to their senses and escape the devil's trap, having been captured alive by him to do his will.|Keeps sobriety, trapping and war-captive images.
3:1|Know this: difficult times will come in the last days.|Retains temporal frame and severity.
3:2|For people will be self-loving, money-loving, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful and unholy,|Keeps compound love terms and complete first list.
3:3|without natural affection, unwilling to reconcile, slanderous, without self-control, brutal and hating what is good,|Preserves every relational and moral descriptor.
3:4|treacherous, reckless, conceited, loving pleasure rather than loving God,|Keeps three traits and the love contrast.
3:5|holding an outward form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from such people.|Preserves appearance/reality contrast and distancing command.

3:6|For among them are those who creep into households and capture vulnerable women burdened with sins and led by various desires,|Keeps predatory intrusion and the source's disparaging diminutive without obscuring victimization.
3:7|always learning yet never able to come to knowledge of the truth.|Retains the perpetual learning/never arriving contrast.

3:8|Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these people oppose the truth—people corrupted in mind and disqualified regarding the faith.|Keeps traditional names, Moses comparison and failed test.
3:9|But they will not advance much further, for their folly will be obvious to everyone, just as the folly of those two became obvious.|Preserves limit and public exposure.
3:10|But you have followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love and endurance,|Keeps the complete sevenfold example.

3:11|as well as my persecutions and sufferings—what happened to me in Antioch, Iconium and Lystra, the persecutions I endured. Yet the Lord rescued me from them all.|Retains all three cities, repeated persecution and deliverance.
3:12|Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.|Keeps the sweeping prediction and Christ setting.
3:13|But evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.|Preserves active/passive deception and moral decline.
3:14|But you, continue in what you learned and became convinced of, knowing from whom you learned it,|Keeps continuity, conviction and plural teachers.
3:15|and how from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which can make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.|Retains infancy, writings and their instrumental ability.

3:16|Every Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, rebuke, correction and training in righteousness,|Keeps God-breathed predicate and all four uses while allowing the punctuation alternative in a note.
3:17|so that the person of God may be capable, fully equipped for every good work.|Preserves fitness and complete preparation.

4:1|I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is going to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom:|Keeps judicial role, both human groups and two future realities.

4:2|Proclaim the word; be ready when the time is favorable or unfavorable; correct, rebuke and encourage, with complete patience and teaching.|Retains urgency in all seasons and three speaking actions.

4:3|For a time will come when people will not tolerate sound teaching. Instead, with itching ears and according to their own desires, they will accumulate teachers for themselves.|Keeps health metaphor, bodily itch and self-selected authorities.
4:4|They will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.|Preserves the matched turning actions.
4:5|But you, remain sober in everything, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist and fulfill your ministry.|Keeps four direct commands and vocational terms.
4:6|For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has arrived.|Retains sacrificial pouring and departure metaphor.
4:7|I have fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith.|Preserves athletic/military sequence and all three completed claims.

4:8|From now on, the crown of righteousness is reserved for me. The Lord, the righteous judge, will award it to me on that day—and not only to me, but also to all who have loved his appearing.|Keeps crown, judge and inclusive future award.
4:9|Make every effort to come to me soon,|Retains urgency and personal need.

4:10|because Demas deserted me, having loved the present age, and went to Thessalonica. Crescens went to Galatia and Titus to Dalmatia.|Preserves all names, destinations and the motive attributed only to Demas.
4:11|Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in ministry.|Keeps Luke's solitude and Mark's changed usefulness.
4:12|I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.|Retains name, action and destination.
4:13|When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas, as well as the scrolls, especially the parchments.|Keeps all concrete items, person and place.
4:14|Alexander the metalworker did me great harm. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.|Retains identity, real harm and entrusts repayment to the Lord.
4:15|You too should watch out for him, because he strongly opposed our words.|Keeps prudent warning and reason.
4:16|At my first defense no one came to stand with me; everyone deserted me. May it not be counted against them.|Preserves abandonment and explicit nonretaliatory prayer.

4:17|But the Lord stood beside me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully made and all the nations might hear. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.|Keeps divine presence, universal hearing and dangerous animal image.
4:18|The Lord will rescue me from every evil deed and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.|Retains confidence, heavenly destination and doxology.
4:19|Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.|Keeps both named coworkers and household.
4:20|Erastus remained in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.|Retains names, places and unresolved illness.
4:21|Make every effort to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the brothers and sisters greet you.|Keeps seasonal urgency and every named greeter.
4:22|The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with all of you.|Preserves singular personal blessing followed by plural community blessing.
